Shri Narsingh Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand on 11
December, 2024

Author: Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi
Bench: Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi
 In The High Court Of Jharkhand, Ranchi
 W.P. (Cr.) No. 484 of 2023
 ----
Shri Narsingh Singh, aged about 73 years, S/o Late Brahma Singh, Proprietor of M/s Narsingh

10/11.12.2024

Heard learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, learned counsel appearing for the respondent State and learned counsel appearing for the Respondent No.2.
2.

The prayer in the writ petition is made for quashing of the entire criminal proceeding including the order taking cognizance dated 30.06.2022 in connection with C.P. sentences.text: The complaint case was filed alleging therein that in the year --1-- W.P. (Cr.) No. 484 of 2023 2017, accused came to the office of the complainant at Dhanbad and dishonestly and fraudulently induced the complainant to supply sandvick rock tools for his mining project at Sekhpura, Bihar.

At the time of entering into the business, accused falsely assured the complaint that he would make the entire payment of the received rock tools in cash or through bank on the same day of receiving the materials.

On the bonafide belief of the words the accused, complainant got stuck in his web and started the business with the accused and supplied the Sandvick rock tools to the accused at his destination and raises the bills as per the order of the accused.

Initially accused made few payments but just after few days, accused started neglecting inn payments of the received materials to the complainant.
When complainant requested the accused that total dues i.e., Rs.4,37,696.00 then accused made the fake promise the entire payment dues will be paid very shortly, but even after the lapse of time accused not paid the dues to the complainant.
On 23.05.2019, complainant for the first time served the advocate notice and requested for the payment and after receiving the notice accused assured the complainant, due to some personal reasons payment was not done and he will make the entire payment very soon.
That even after, lapse of one year accused neither paid the dues amount nor tried to contact with the complainant, in fact complainant sent his legal representative several time and made several phone calls and requested to make the payment but accused --3-- W.P. (Cr.) No. 484 of 2023 intentionally not paying the dues to the complainant.

sentences.text: Again on 29.09.2020 complainant served the demand notice through speed post to the accused and notice was delivered to the accused but even after receiving the notice, accused not responded anything to the complainant.

Accused have intention of deception from the very beginning and that is why firstly accused induced the complainant to enter into the business and later on intentionally with the malafide intention not paid the dues amount i.e. Rs.4,37,696.00 to the complainant till today.
Accused dishonestly induced the complainant and deceived the complainant to deliver the material in his destination.
Based Upon which a Complaint Case vide C. P. Case No. 2080 of 2020 was brought by the complainant.

sentences.text: Pursuant to Complaint petition, cognizance was taken under sections 420 and 406 of Indian Penal Code by Ld. Court of Nirbhay Prakash, JMFC, Dhanbad vide order dated 30.06.2022 4.
Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is engaged in business of various sector including the business of stone.

He has several stones sites across the State of Bihar,
where work goes on throughout the year.

During the course of business, complainant approached the petitioner with an offer to supply rock tools, which are regularly required at the stone crushing sites, where heavy machines are used for crushing the stones.
He submits that the complainant and the petitioner are in business terms and for that several times the tools were purchased.

He submits that in paragraph No.5 the amount of supplied rock tools have been disclosed --4-- W.P. (Cr.) No. 484 of 2023 and it is stated that about Rs.4,37,696/- is not paid and for that the case has been registered.
He submits that the petitioner has made a payment of Rs.25,38,000/- that has been stated in paragraph No.11 of the writ petition.

He submits that in this background no criminal case is made out and even if the case is made out for recovery of money and for that the criminal case has been filed which is not maintainable and the cognizance has been taken under Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

He submits that both the sections cannot be the subject matter of the cognizance on the same set of facts in light of judgment of Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of Delhi Race Club (1940) Ltd. and Others versus State of Uttar Pradesh and Another reported in (2024) SCC OnLine 2248 in paragraph No.43 it has been held as under:-
43.

entities.text: Delhi Race Club (1940) Ltd. and Others versus State of Uttar Pradesh and Another reported in (2024) SCC OnLine 2248
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the police officers across the country are imparted proper training in law so as to understand the fine distinction between the offence of cheating viz-a-viz criminal breach of trust.
Both offences are independent and distinct.
The two offences cannot coexist simultaneously in the same set of facts.
They are antithetical to each other.
The two provisions of the IPC (now BNS, 2023) are not twins that they cannot survive without each other.

He further submits that in the same judgment in paragraph Nos.10 to 13 and 24 to 30 it has been further held that if the goods is supplied and payment is not made then the only remedy is for filing of the suit in terms of the Sales of Goods Act.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent State submits that on the complaint case the learned Court has been pleased to take --5-- W.P. (Cr.) No. 484 of 2023 cognizance.

6. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 submits that the learned Court after looking into the enquiry witnesses has been pleased to take cognizance and the case is made out and in view of that this Court may not interfere at this stage.
He relied in the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajesh Bajaj versus State NCT of Delhi and Others reported in (1999) 3 SCC 259.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above submission of learned counsel appearing for the parties and looking into the contents of the complaint petition it is crystal clear that for recovery of a sum of Rs.4,37,696/- the present case has been lodged.

The total supply of goods is said to be of Rs.21,74,510/- meaning thereby major amount has already been paid wherein it has been contended in paragraph No.11 of the writ petition that the petitioner has paid a sum of Rs.25,38,000/-.
Thus, it is crystal clear from the very beginning the intention to cheat is not there which is one of the ingredients to make out a case of cheating.

8. In the case of Delhi Race Club (1940) Ltd. (supra) it has been held that a particular amount is due and payable to the complainant then he should have filed a civil suit for recovery of the amount against the accused and going to the criminal court for filing a complaint of cheating and criminal breach of trust is bad.

9. There is no doubt that if the criminality is made out in civil and criminal both cases can be maintained, however, if the criminality is not made out to allow the proceeding will amount to abuse of process of law.

10. It is further well settled that every breach of contract would not give rise to an offence of cheating and only in those cases breach of --6-- W.P. (Cr.) No. 484 of 2023 contract would amount to cheating where there was any deception played at the very inception that is lacking in the case.

Reference may be made to the case of Vesa Holdings Pvt. Limited & Anr. versus State of Kerala & Ors. reported in (2015) 8 SCC 293.
11.

entities.text: Vesa Holdings Pvt. Limited & Anr. versus State of Kerala & Ors. reported in (2015) 8 SCC 293
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far the judgment relied by Mr. Lukesh Kumar, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 in the case of Rajesh Bajaj (supra) is concerned in that case the inception was made from the very beginning and not even a pie was paid and on that fact the order has been passed and the facts of the present case is otherwise.
It is a clear case of recovery of Rs.4,37,696/- and major payment has already been paid.

12. In view of the above facts, reasons and analysis to allow the proceeding to continue will amount to abuse of process of law, as such the entire criminal proceeding including the order taking cognizance dated 30.06.2022 in connection with C.P. Case No.2080 of 2020 pending in the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Dhanbad is hereby quashed.
13. This petition is allowed and disposed of.

(Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.)
Sangam/
 A.F.R.
